correctness.rationale: For fixed s>0 write a+sZ=R exp(iΘ) under the stated circular Gaussian normalization. Differentiation under the expectation is justified by the pointwise bounded displacement derivative of the norm away from a null event. Using E[R cosΘ]=a, the derivative of Var(R)=a²+s²−(ER)² is 2 Cov(R,cosΘ). Polar conditioning gives density proportional to exp(2ar cosθ/s²), so the derivative of E[cosΘ|R=r] in r is (2a/s²)Var(cosΘ|R=r)>0 for a>0. The independent-copy covariance identity proves strict monotonicity for a>0. At a=0 the Rayleigh variance is s²(1−π/4), giving (ER)²≤a²+c²s², with equality only on the two axes, including s=0 directly. Gaussian unitary invariance reduces any affine F to A+sZ with A=|a|, s=‖b‖₂ and r=‖F‖₂=√(A²+s²). The squared difference between the chord c r+(1−c)A and the preceding square-root upper bound is 2c(1−c)A(r−A) in the sense of difference of their squares. Thus the chord bound is strictly improved in every mixed case. Expanding the two squared distances using ∫F=a proves the radial inequality and axis equality cases. The unit pure linear wave has squared phase distance 2 and squared modulus distance 2−√π, forcing the exact Lipschitz constant; equality at positive distance in that bound additionally requires r=1. Constants of nonunit norm saturate the radial remainder, so its coefficient cannot be raised with the phase-distance coefficient fixed. Direct numerical evaluation of the exact constant agreed with the printed decimal 2.9646965828533536. Inspected the 64-point Bessel checker, not executed; the replay of the global claim is the analytic covariance and chord proof, not its finite grid.
